new_statements.quote: NASALIZAÇÃO: Todas as vogais podem ser nasalizadas e quando o forem receberão um til (~). SÍLABA TÔNICA: Na maioria das vezes, é a última sílaba da palavra. Por isso, só usamos o acento quando ele recai em outra sílaba. Acentuamos também o hiato (ex.: aí). Acentuamos a primeira vogal de ditongo com vogal nasal, quando esta não fôr a acentuada (ex.: éĩ).
new_statements.translation: NASALIZATION: All vowels can be nasalized and when they are they receive a tilde (~). STRESSED SYLLABLE: In most cases it is the last syllable of the word. For that reason we write the accent mark only when it falls on another syllable. We also mark hiatus (e.g. aí). We put an accent on the first vowel of a diphthong with a nasal vowel when that vowel is not the stressed one (e.g. éĩ).

new_statements.rule_in_words: Word stress falls on the final syllable in the majority of the 129 recorded words; non-final stress occurs in a minority of items and is marked in the practical orthography with a written accent.
new_statements.exceptions: 'Na maioria das vezes' -- some words have stress on a non-final syllable; these are the ones written with an accent mark in the booklet's word pages (no list or count given in the criteria text).
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level ('sílaba da palavra'); based on isolated citation forms (129 words, 2 sentences) elicited from a single elderly rememberer (Bahetá, Itaju do Colônia, Bahia, 1982; researchers G. Urban and A. Lopes da Silva; orthography by E. P. Orlandi at IEL/Unicamp from the phonetic transcriptions and tapes). An orthography note, not a phonological analysis.
new_statements.identity_note: Statement concerns Pataxó Hãhãhãe proper (pata1261, 'Pataxó Setentrional'), as remembered by the last speaker Bahetá in 1982 (129 words, 2 sentences) -- not the revitalized Patxohã used today by the Pataxó people (which Nikulin 2020 treats as unclassifiable) and not Wied's Pataxó Meridional. The source is an orthography-criteria note in a community booklet, written by a linguist (E. P. Orlandi) from phonetic transcriptions and tapes; it is first-hand but not a phonological analysis, and the corpus is terminal-speaker citation forms.
